findings.finding: The +/-85 deg fan means preaching to a congregation spread over about 170 deg. 320 seats sit more than 75 deg off the pulpit axis and see the preacher in near-profile, or the back, whenever he addresses the centre. The end seats of the front rows sit almost level with the pulpit, beside the platform.
findings.evidence: config/params.json seating.fan_half_angle_deg 85.0; comparison.md max bearing from pulpit 85.0 deg, 320 seats > 75 deg; open_issues.md ('preaching to a 170 deg fan needs a speaker who turns'); renders/B01-5f175dba4d/04b_interior_from_side_seats.png.
findings.fix: Reduce the fan to about +/-70-75 deg and recover the seats with one or two extra rows (the fan study notes +/-80 deg needs 33 rows). Alternatively, move the platform focus F 2-3 m further into the room (deeper thrust) so the side blocks wrap round the pulpit rather than sit beside it.

findings.finding: The choir provision is weak and remote: 263 chairs (A has 386), placed in the two front corners at floor level behind the 85 deg side blocks. The far chairs are about 20 m from the platform, the choir is barely visible to the congregation, and choir-to-band contact is poor. The client's choir preference was carried over from A, not re-approved.
findings.evidence: comparison.md choir chairs 263 vs 386; config/params.json stage.choir.target_chairs 380 vs metrics choir_seats 263; space_schedule.csv SP-03/SP-04 Front corner (choir / platform access) 193.32 m2 each; floor_plan.png (purple blocks x about 3-24 m and 56-77 m); 04_interior_from_rear.png.
findings.fix: Move the choir onto tiered risers on the platform's rear band either side of the band (widen the band 26 m to about 34-36 m with 4-5 risers), or onto raised choir lofts against the stage wall. Confirm the target choir size with the client before freezing B.

findings.finding: There is no ministry or altar-call floor. The seating wraps the semicircular thrust with only the 3.0 m front clear zone, which is also the front cross passage and egress route. Altar calls, communion lines and praise dancing would block an exit route, and the pulpit thrust leaves no space for people to come forward.
findings.evidence: config/params.json seating.front_clear_zone 3.0 and 'front clear zone ... doubles as the front cross passage'; stage.thrust_radius 5.5; metrics.rejected_candidates 'platform front clear zone' 34; 03_interior_from_platform.png (front rows close to the thrust edge). A has a dedicated 117 m2 SP-02F.
findings.fix: Remove the inner one or two rows of the centre blocks (about 60-80 seats, recovered at the rear) to create a 6-8 m deep arc-shaped ministry floor in front of the thrust, separate from the egress passage. Model it as a named IfcSpace.

findings.finding: Entrance sequence: everyone arrives at the 10 m deep ground foyer and must climb 2.98 m (about 17 risers) up two 6 m stairs to the rear passage, then walk down the rake. The two side foyers are residual triangles left by the fan at the rear corners: one is reached through a single corner door and corner stairs and holds the main toilets, away from the main foyer. The arrival is functional but not a gathering experience, and the residual corners read as left-overs.
findings.evidence: space_schedule.csv SP-06 Main foyer 861.36 m2, SP-05W/E side foyers 244.63 m2 each; levels L02 +2.980; ARC-STAIR-FOYER-E/W, ARC-STAIR-CORNER-E/W; floor_plan.png (CORNER-W/E doors, toilets in rear corners); section_AA.png.
findings.fix: Sink the front rows (or the foyer) so the main foyer is at rear-passage level, letting arrivals walk in level and see the platform on entry. Alternatively put grand ramped entries in the side foyers, give them daylight and a direct door from the main foyer, and make them deliberate courts (welcome / cafe / bookshop) rather than left-overs.

findings.finding: The sound / media booth (24 m2) is 3.3 m off the centre axis because a truss crosses the axis, and it is smaller than A's 43.65 m2 booth. Off-axis mixing gives an unbalanced stereo / centre image across a 170 deg fan. Its view over the rear passage (+2.98) from a floor at +3.18 will be blocked by standing people.
findings.evidence: manifest ARC-BOOTH matrix x 43.30, y -2.70, z 3.18 (platform axis x 40.0); config/params.json foyer.booth x [40.4, 46.2] and its _note; open_issues.md 'Booth sits 0.4-6.2 m east of the centre line'; space_schedule.csv SP-08 24.36 m2.
findings.fix: Shift the truss grid by half a bay (4 m) so that a bay, not a truss, falls on the axis, and centre the booth on x = 40. Raise the booth floor to at least 1.0 m above the rear passage, or put a front-of-house mix position in the cross aisle, and enlarge it to about 40 m2.

findings.finding: The platform is undersized for the 80 m wall and the band. Its 26 x 5.5 m rear band (about 143 m2 plus a 47.5 m2 thrust) is shallow for drums, keys, monitors and risers, and reads small against the 80 m stage wall.
findings.evidence: config/params.json stage.rear_band_width 26.0, rear_band_depth 5.5, thrust_radius 5.5; metrics platform_area 190.5; renders 04_interior_from_rear.png.
findings.fix: Deepen the rear band to 7-8 m (the stage wall can move north into the back-of-house corridor zone) and widen it to about 34 m, giving the band and choir risers room. Frame it with a stage-wall feature.

findings.finding: The massing is a single 90 x 75 m mono-pitch plane rising away from the entrance. The low eave and a long flat canopy face the arrival side, and the tallest wall (about 14 m) faces the service side. From outside it reads as a flat warehouse roof with no civic or church identity. Glazing totals only 94 m2.
findings.evidence: renders/B01-5f175dba4d/01_exterior_aerial.png; section_AA.png (roof rising from grid 1 to grid 4); comparison.md roof area 6,355 m2, roof top 14.2 m, glazing 94.3 m2, footprint 6,774 m2 (24% larger than A).
findings.fix: Consider reversing the pitch so the high eave faces the entrance, or add a raised entrance volume / clerestory lantern over the foyer stairs and an identity element (tower, cross, perforated screen). Glaze the foyer facade fully under a deep overhang.

findings.finding: Inside, the wide fan under a rising roof is spatially promising and intimate, but the stage wall is a blank 80 m elevation with exposed X-bracing either side of the platform, and the roof is exposed trusses throughout.
findings.evidence: renders/B01-5f175dba4d/04_interior_from_rear.png (bracing visible on the stage wall); open_issues.md (acoustic infill above the faceted rear-passage wall not modelled).
findings.fix: Move the stage-wall bracing bays to the outer bays or behind a lining, and model a stage-wall feature and acoustic lining.

findings.finding: Only an upper lift door (DR-LIFT-L02) is modelled; no ground-level lift door object was found, so I could not confirm the step-free arrival route from the foyer to the rear passage in the model.
findings.evidence: model/blender_manifest.json: DR-LIFT-L02 present, no DR-LIFT-L00 (A has both DR-LIFT-L00 and DR-LIFT-L02); SP-09 Lift shaft 5.76 m2.
findings.fix: Add the L00 lift door, a landing and a clear approach in the main foyer. Consider a second lift or a ramp for 3,000 occupants.

strengths: Much better proximity and engagement than A: 31 rows, mean pulpit distance 27.3 m, max 39.5 m (A: 35.5 / 57.6 m), and no seat beyond 40 m (comparison.md; own manifest measurement, min 5.16 m).
Concentric rows face the platform focus: mean head turn 5.1 deg, max 23.7 deg, 0 seats > 30 deg (A: 670). The congregation sees itself, which supports a communal, participatory worship character.
A generous main foyer (861 m2) plus two 245 m2 side foyers and larger toilet allowances (74 m2 each), about 1,350 m2 of foyer in total against about 1,090 m2 in A.
A lower rake (highest seat floor +2.98 against A's +4.28) gives a shorter climb and less reliance on upper-level circulation.
One roof plane over foyer and hall, rising towards the platform, is internally logical and avoids box gutters (params.json foyer._proposal).
The back-of-house strip (vestry, prayer room, green room, band store at stage level) sits directly behind the platform.
limitations: Scores cover only architecture (15%), church_functionality (15%) and aesthetics (5%). weighted_score = 2.10 is the partial contribution of these three disciplines (35% of total weight); normalised to 0-10 it is 6.0. I did not inspect the .blend or IFC directly. Measurements are from blender_manifest.json, params.json, the schedules and comparison.md. I could not verify the booth sightline over standing occupants, the choir sightlines, or the side-foyer level relationships beyond the drawings. No site or orientation data were available. The aesthetic judgement is based on the grey-box renders.
